messages:
mira: FYI customer acme-finance reporting a spike in 504s + P99 latency after upgrading to go-sdk v0.10.2 ~11:10 UTC. Logs show a mix of "context canceled" and "http: request canceled" during retries. They say it only shows up under sustained load behind their HAProxy layer.

support-bot: Alert forwarded to #support: acme-finance - elevated 5xx and latency.

oscar: Thanks. Can you paste a minimal repro? Is it definitely the SDK level retry logic or could it be a proxy/tcp keepalive issue? Any HTTP/2 in the path?

mira: Pasting a trimmed repro they sent (obfuscated):

```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()

req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", client.Endpoint+"/v1/generate", bytes.NewReader(payload))
// using SDK that wraps http.Client under the hood
resp, err := httpClient.Do(req)
if err != nil {
    log.Printf("do error: %v", err)
    return
}
body, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
resp.Body.Close()
```

Error lines from their kube logs: `http: request canceled`, `context canceled`, and occasional `net/http: timeout awaiting response headers`. Happens after several minutes of steady traffic.

ramya: Two likely things: (1) context deadline vs http.Client.Timeout race — if both are used they can cancel mid-read; (2) connection reuse + premature cancel -> reused connection in pool gets closed and next request gets weird errors. Are they setting Transport.MaxIdleConnsPerHost / IdleConnTimeout? Which Go runtime?

oscar: Also ask if they upgraded Go runtime alongside SDK. net/http changed some behavior around connection reuse in go1.19->1.20. If they have HTTP/2 and proxy in front it can exacerbate.

ali: Quick workaround to validate transport behavior: set custom transport:

```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100,
  IdleConnTimeout: 30 * time.Second,
  DisableKeepAlives: false,
  ForceAttemptHTTP2: false, // toggle to see if HTTP/2 is contributing
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
```

If the spike disappears with ForceAttemptHTTP2=false or with DisableKeepAlives=true it points to connection reuse / http2 race. Note DisableKeepAlives=true removes pooling cost but increases latency/cost.

oscar: Another important angle — SDK v0.10.x introduced an aggressive per-request cancel on deadline to avoid stuck goroutines. That change can race with transport reuses. We have a patch in v0.10.3 that delays cancel until Body.Close finishes for successful responses. Can we confirm their SDK version?

mira: Customer says sdk.version header X-SDK-Version: 0.10.2 and Go runtime go1.20.8. They run on GKE with HAProxy sidecar.

ramya: That combo is suspicious. HAProxy + http2 + go1.20 + the new SDK cancel semantics -> higher chance of races. Ask them to try either: (A) upgrade SDK to 0.10.3 (if available) or (B) temporary transport tweak: ForceAttemptHTTP2=false and increase MaxIdleConnsPerHost. Also verify they are not using http.Client.Timeout in addition to context timeouts.

jason: Please open a private escalation ticket with full request IDs, the exact request latency traces, and kube node logs. We should also try to reproduce in our lab with a haproxy+http2 setup and SDK 0.10.2. If repro is quick, we can provide a hotfix/backport.

mira: Action items:
1) Ask acme-finance to try SDK v0.10.3 or the transport workaround (ForceAttemptHTTP2=false) and report results.
2) Gather a few request IDs and paste the exact log snippets and timestamps.
3) Oscar to attempt a local repro using go1.20 + haproxy + sdk v0.10.2.

oscar: I'll take repro, ETA today EOD.

mira: Thanks — I'll message the customer with the two workarounds and open the support case. :pray:
